_comment: The reading-SELECTION baseline -- a SEPARATE experiment from the parse baseline (baseline.json). The parse baseline gates the GRAMMAR + lexicon: what forest is produced (the pins ask whether the correct STRUCTURE survives). THIS file gates the RANKER: which reading gets chosen from that forest, scored READING-level (structure + word senses) against the adjudication ledger. Different re-baselining triggers: grammar work re-draws the parse baseline without touching this file; a new selection draw, a prompt change, or a ledger revision re-derives THIS baseline without touching the parse numbers. Update deliberately, never to make a red run go green.

provenance.date: 2026-09-30 (eigenius#264 strand 1: the two-call reading ranker, branch prepositions-and-ranker)
provenance.forest: ranks experiments/parsing/ranks/2026-09-29-d95-slice8.json, which replay against this snapshot with 62 hits, 0 misses
provenance.selections: experiments/parsing/selections/2026-09-30-ranker-twocall-v2-1.json, the first two-call draw of the A/B; replay 41 hits, 0 misses

gates.reading_unadjudicated: GATED: must be 0 on the tracked replay -- an unadjudicated decision makes the number a partial count, not a measurement; a new draw choosing novel readings fails until its ledger rows are adjudicated (mirrors audit-skeletons).
gates.invalid_selected: GATED: must be 0 (SELECTION-VALIDITY). The ranker has no kernel veto -- every candidate type-checks -- so the ledger and this validity check are its controls.
gates.structure_correct: diagnostic only -- reported, never gated; the pins belong to the parse baseline's faithfulness gate.
gates.ledger_conflicts: GATED: must be 0 (LEDGER, eval-parse-rate.sh). A `correct` ledger row whose reading the forest produces must have its pin's structure or say `departs`; the sweep audits every produced row, chosen or not.
gates.reading_conflict: Reported: chosen readings on a conflicting row, counted as neither correct nor wrong. Zero whenever ledger_conflicts is.

_provenance_note_2026-08-22b-production-: RE-MEASURED after the #210/#205 close-out (2026-08-22, commit a05cfa1, snapshot wordnet-umls-aligned-2026-08-22c). Tracked draw: ranks/2026-08-22-productiontrace.json, selections/2026-08-22-productiontrace-live.json. Live and replay AGREE. Coverage: grammar-gap 0, expected-hits 62/62, miss-set unchanged, skeletons 170 (unchanged). Selection: 41 eligible, 30 correct, 0 unadjudicated, 0 invalid-selected — reading-correct 30/40 -> 30/41, holds. total-readings 613 -> 674, ungated and inside the 700 ceiling. ONE ADJUDICATION was needed to reach 0 unadjudicated: «The MSI relationship compared favourably…» chose a reading structurally IDENTICAL to two rows already ruled `wrong` for that unit (the conjunction split, hanging «for vulnerabilities» on the subject), and wrong on both contested sense axes besides. Recorded `wrong`. METHOD, after getting it wrong earlier the same day: a single live run is a DRAW, not a measurement. Draw until clean (up to 3), PROMOTE the clean draw to ranks/, replay it to confirm live and replay agree, and only then read the numbers. Four earlier draws that day reported 61 hits twice on DIFFERENT sentences; two of them carried malformed sense-ranker replies (eigenius#212), and none had been promoted. Check `grep -c 'malformed reply'` before attributing any delta to code.

_provenance_note_2026-09-29-d95-slices-6: D95 SLICES 6-8 — MEASURED, NOT ADOPTED: `provenance` and `expected` above still describe the 2026-09-29-d95-quantities draw, pending the maintainer's ruling on reading_correct. The tracked draw for the slice 6-8 forest is selections/2026-09-29-d95-slice8.json over ranks/2026-09-29-d95-slice8.json (snapshot wordnet-umls-aligned-2026-09-29-quantities-s8b, commit 7df7bce): recorded live, 0 malformed replies, and replayed with 41 hits and 0 misses. A new draw was required: slices 7a and 7d changed the candidate pools of four eligible units, and the selection key includes the glosses of the page's earlier selections (reading_ranker.rs, selection_key), so with the page's first unit among the four no later key of the old recording can match. It scores reading-correct 29/41 against the expected 30, wrong 12, unadjudicated 0 (six ledger rows added), invalid-selected 0, structure-correct 34 (33). The decisions that changed, on the four new pools: «The four other RecQ DNA helicases …» wrong -> correct (`the four` takes `four` out of the compound, so the UMLS qualifier-junk nouns for `other` are no longer offered); «Synthetic lethality is an interaction between two genetic events.» correct -> wrong (`genetic` a02734192, the sense the ledger already ruled wrong for this sentence in an earlier draw); «We analysed two …» wrong -> wrong; «We identified three …» correct -> correct. On pools identical to the old draw's: «Many cancers exhibit an impairment of a DNA repair pathway.» and «Some cancers do not respond to immune checkpoint blockade.» correct -> wrong, «The use of immune checkpoint blockade can be limited by toxicity.» wrong -> correct. Those pools did not change, but each decision's prompt carries the page's earlier selections (resolver_llm.rs), and «Synthetic lethality …», whose selection changed, is the page's first unit. Net 30 + 1 - 1 - 1 = 29. THE LEDGER CONTRADICTS ITS OWN RULE on three rows that score these draws (found 2026-09-30): its header rules a chosen structure contradicting the verified pin `wrong` with no sense judgment needed, but line 89 rules `correct` the reading of «Some cancers do not respond to immune checkpoint blockade.» with `to` as a free VP adjunct — the competitor the pin's note rejects, and the structure line 49 rules wrong on those grounds — and lines 98 and 138 rule `correct` two readings of «We queried dependencies in cancers with MSI.» that attach `with MSI` to the dependencies, which the pin's note rejects as asserting that the dependencies carry MSI. With those three rows `wrong`, the old draw and this one both score 28. The maintainer's options: correct the three rows and set expected.reading_correct to 28 (a ledger revision is one of this file's re-derivation triggers); set 29 with the ledger as it stands; draw again; or keep 30. _provenance_note_2026-09-30-ledger-check: RE-DERIVED from a ledger revision (one of this file's triggers), on the maintainer's rulings of 2026-09-30. THE RULE: a reading whose structure differs from its pin cannot count as correct, and a row that contradicts another row's ruling on the same sentence is flagged. Each `wrong` ledger row now names what it rules out (a fifth field: `structure`, `sense <atom>...`), and a `correct` row off its pin says `departs`; `reading_ledger_is_consistent` and the sweep reject cross-row contradictions, and the sweep audits every row its forest produces (ledger_conflicts, gated to 0). The checks found 19 `correct` rows that could not stand and 3 `wrong` rows whose ground did not hold. The maintainer's rulings on the open ones: C0600688 «Toxic effect» is a faithful twin of n13583478 for «toxicity» (its NCI definition: the finding of bodily harm due to the poisonous effects of something); `arise` v02625786 and v02624263 are near-synonym twins; need-claims (essential, dispensable, dependency, dependent on) take the WRN PROTEIN kind, not the gene — what a cell needs to survive is the protein's activity, even when a screen shows it by deleting the gene. Seven pins moved to the protein kind, the seventh on the follow-up ruling that «WRN is a promising drug target» means the protein (baseline.json's note of the same date); the drug-target unit is open, so no selection figure moved. THIS DRAW, 29 -> 25 (replayed at ea85d49, 41 hits, 0 misses): «We queried dependencies in cancers with MSI.» correct -> wrong (both PPs on «dependencies»; the pin nests «with MSI» in «cancers»); «We found that WRN was selectively essential in MSI models.», «WRN was dispensable in models of microsatellite-stable cancers.» and «We evaluated MSI as a biomarker for WRN dependency.» correct -> wrong (the gene individual in a need-claim). structure-correct 33 -> 30 for the same three: the pins now have the protein.
